en: The Philippines consists of 7,641 islands, making it over 500 islands larger than the previously estimated count of 7,107.
Standing at 2,954 meters, Mount Apo is the highest peak in the Philippines, surpassing Mount Pulag's height of 2,928 meters.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River stretches 8.2 kilometers, making it one of the longest navigable underground rivers in the world.
Covering 340 square kilometers, Lake Lanao is the largest lake in Mindanao, significantly bigger than Lake Mainit's 169 square kilometers.
The Philippine Trench plunges to a depth of 10,540 meters, making it the third deepest ocean trench in the world.
More than half of the Philippines' 200 native mammal species, including the Philippine eagle, are endemic and found nowhere else on Earth.
Baguio City receives an average annual rainfall of 4,000 millimeters, which is double the typical 2,000-millimeter average experienced in other regions.
The Philippines is the world's fifth-largest nickel producer, mining over 300,000 metric tons of nickel ore each year.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park covers 97,030 hectares, making it the largest and most pristine marine protected area in the Philippines.
Stretching 505 kilometers, the Cagayan River is the longest in the Philippines, significantly longer than the 350-kilometer Agusan River.
Luzon covers 109,965 square kilometers, making it significantly larger than Mindanao, which is the second-largest island at 97,530 square kilometers.
The 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo ejected 10 cubic kilometers of material, making it the second-largest volcanic eruption of the 20th century.
